closed_slices.plane: ODK surface descriptors, data recipes, and manifests
closed_slices.bounded_scope: The ODK authoring plane's create/patch/delete only. No claim about DomainApp mount, serve, package admission, extension-application registration, or System binding.
evidence: CLOSED. All seven ODK mutations — surface-descriptor create/patch/delete, data-recipe create/patch, and odk-manifest create/patch — share ONE owner-scoped admission path (odk_admit): authenticated identity, owner binding, required caller idempotency_key, expected-head compare-and-swap on every successor, Agentgres admission, and a returned receipt_ref. Resource identity is derived from owner+idempotency_key rather than wall-clock, so a retry resolves the same resource; wall-clock is excluded from the admitted payload entirely and projected onto the read model from the admission. DELETE is a recorded tombstone successor rather than a silent row drop, and the read-model row is removed only after the tombstone is durable. Descriptor GET surfaces admitted_head so a caller can compare-and-swap.

closed_slices.bounded_scope: The ADMISSION of a planner decision only: identity, owner scope, idempotency, durable admission, receipt. No claim that any admitted decision is EXECUTED.
evidence: CLOSED for the admission boundary. All THIRTEEN kernel-planner endpoints in lifecycle_routes.rs — every handler that previously returned a bare 202 with a planned record and persisted nothing — now authenticate the caller BEFORE the planner runs, require owner_ref and idempotency_key, derive admission identity from owner+key rather than wall-clock, admit the planner's record through admit_owner_scoped_mutation, and return receipt_ref plus operation_ref. Verified live on all 13 routes: 401 unauthenticated, typed refusals when authenticated. STILL OPEN and explicitly NOT claimed here: extension_application registration, executable artifact activation, product-catalog/System/serving bindings, upgrade, rollback, and affected-System remediation — those are the EXECUTION of an admitted decision, not its admission.

closed_slices.plane: Domain App records, runtimes, mount receipts, serve state, and kill-switch enforcement
closed_slices.bounded_scope: The ADMISSION and ordering of Domain App state transitions. No claim that a mounted runtime executes anything: this plane still starts no process, exposes no URL, and generates no app code.
evidence: CLOSED. All seven Domain App mutations (create, patch, delete, mount, unmount, serve, stop-serving) plus governance kill enforcement now authenticate the caller as their FIRST statement, require owner_ref and idempotency_key, and admit one canonical transition through the shared owner-scoped write path before any projection write. Create derives its resource id from owner+idempotency_key instead of `nanos()`, so a retried create resolves to the one resource it already made rather than minting a second. Every successor presents the head it read; a record written before this plane bound identity is refused rather than silently advanced.

The mount/unmount/serve/stop-serving fan-out — a runtime record, a Domain App backlink, and N receipts — now admits the transition ahead of all three writes. Previously the only crash story was rollback, so a process death between writes left no durable trace of the attempt; the admitted transition is now the recoverable intent.

Kill enforcement was reachable UNAUTHENTICATED and enforced runtime-by-runtime, returning on the first failure: with five targets, a failure at the third left two runtimes killed, three running, and the KillSwitch never updated — a half-enforced kill that no record described. It now authenticates, admits one transition naming every target runtime before stopping any of them, and on partial failure returns the admitted head plus the planned and already-enforced target lists so recovery can finish the set instead of guessing it.

Proven against a live daemon, not only in tests: 401 on all seven mutations and on kill-enforce while unauthenticated; typed mutation_owner_ref_required and mutation_idempotency_key_invalid when authenticated; identity refused before body validation; content-derived id (dapp_74ef08dc370df3e6); an identical retry replaying to that same id with replayed=true; the admitted head advancing across a patch; and cross-tenant owner substitution refused 403 request_tenant_authority_required.
still_open: Mount admission remains governed by an ApprovalRequest plus ReleaseControl but does not itself execute a runtime.
Kill enforcement covers only domain-app-runtime:// and domain-app:// targets. Wallet grants, leases, connectors, environments and workers are out of this cut and are NOT enforced by a tripped switch.

closed_slices.plane: marketplace listings, publish candidates, admission reviews, publish, and managed-instance offers
closed_slices.bounded_scope: The ADMISSION and ordering of marketplace object transitions. The plane's own hard boundaries are unchanged and NOT claimed here: no payments, no settlement, no install/hire runtime, no managed-instance instantiation, no external ingress. `published` still means read-only discoverable metadata with runtime backing.
evidence: CLOSED. All twelve mutations — create, patch and delete across listings, candidates, reviews and offers, plus publish — now authenticate first, require owner_ref and idempotency_key, derive create ids from owner+key rather than nanos(), and admit one canonical transition per mutation. Patches and deletes previously returned a bare Json<Value> with no way to express 401 or 409 at all; they now carry real status codes. Zero discarded persist results remain in the file.

Publish was three discarded writes — receipt, candidate, listing — behind an unconditional 201. A failed receipt write still left the candidate advertising a receipt_ref no read resolved, and a failed candidate write still left the listing public. It is now ONE admitted transition over the whole tuple, projected with checked writes. It also silently skipped the listing flip when the listing no longer resolved, returning 201 with the candidate published and nothing publicly listed; that now refuses with marketplace_publish_listing_missing.

link_candidate_review swallowed every failure and returned unit — malformed ref, missing candidate, failed write alike. publish_gates reads admission_review_ref, so a silent failure there decided publish eligibility from a backlink that was never written. It now returns Result and both callers fail closed.

Two defects were found by live probe AFTER the tests passed, which is why the probe exists: create payloads carried iso_now(), so an identical retry admitted different bytes under the same key and was refused instead of replayed — the idempotency contract was present but inert; and cross-tenant callers received a body-validation 400 rather than 403 because owner authorization ran after body validation. Owner authorization now happens in require_write_caller, before any field is read, which fixes it for every plane on the shared path.

Proven against a live daemon: 401 on all twelve mutations unauthenticated; typed refusals for both missing fields; 403 request_tenant_authority_required on owner substitution; content-derived id mlist_bd490a501b7b5faf; an identical retry replaying to that same id with replayed=true and 200 rather than a second 201; the admitted head advancing across a patch; and publish of an unresolvable candidate refusing typed. 23 of 23 assertions.

open_gaps.gap: 269 direct persist_record results are explicitly discarded across 40 daemon source files (was 304/41; three closed in resource_routes::handle_allocate, the rest by earlier work). This remains a SOURCE INDICATOR, not a defect count. Every occurrence still needs an explicit durable / compensated / best-effort classification.
acceptance: classify every indicator as canonical mutation, derived projection, rollback cleanup, or intentionally best-effort telemetry
migrate canonical mutations to the shared admission boundary or record an owner-approved equivalent
make every projection and cleanup failure observable and recoverable according to its classification
open_gaps.classification_method: A regex census over handler bodies is a LEAD, not a finding. Slicing each `pub(crate) async fn handle_*` body and asking whether it contains any checked write flags ~129 handlers as 'only persistence is discarded' — but that over-counts: lifecycle_routes::handle_secret_create is flagged and does have an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR path. The discriminator that actually holds is narrower: does the handler RETURN SUCCESS carrying a record whose only write was discarded, and is that record READ BACK as authoritative state elsewhere? Confirm both before calling a site a defect.
open_gaps.worked_example: resource_routes::handle_allocate met both tests and is CLOSED. It built an allocation decision with a receipt_ref, discarded the persist, and returned it unconditionally, while handle_* reads allocation-decisions back as admitted state — so a caller could hold a receipted decision no later read would find. It also discarded the budget spend write, silently under-counting spend so the next request saw headroom that did not exist, and the allocation request write, leaving a decision referencing an unfindable request. All three now fail closed with typed 500s.

open_gaps.plane: managed worker runtime, backup, and restore
open_gaps.gap: This plane already has authenticated resource scopes plus direct Agentgres CAS/idempotency for its main state records, but it does not use the shared boundary. Restore cancellation removes staging before the cancelled transition is admitted; restore apply mutates workspace/rollback bytes before the completed transition. Admission failure after those effects can leave state and filesystem posture divergent. Legacy backup projections remain a second fallible write after canonical admission.
acceptance: adopt the shared boundary or prove a byte-equivalent owner-scoped admission wrapper
introduce explicit intent/effect/observation/recovery states for restore filesystem changes
retain rollback material until completion admission is confirmed or record a cleanup obligation
prove cancellation/apply interruption recovery and exact retry after restart
progress: The two effect-ordering defects named in the gap text are FIXED. Restore cancel admitted the cancellation only AFTER deleting the staged bytes: if that append then failed, the plan still read 'prepared' over bytes that were gone, and no reader could tell it was unsatisfiable. Cancel now admits a `restore_plan_cancelling` intent first, so a failure between intent and effect is resumable.

Restore apply deleted the rollback directory — the only copy of the pre-restore workspace — BEFORE admitting completion. A failure in that window left the plan 'applying', the workspace already restored, and nothing left to undo it with: the one state from which neither finishing nor rolling back is possible. Completion is now admitted while the rollback material still exists, and a failure to remove it afterwards is reported as a retained-material cleanup obligation rather than a 500 over a restore that did complete.

`restore_effects_are_admitted_before_they_are_performed` pins both orderings. It asserts source order rather than driving a real restore, because forcing a rename or remove_dir_all to fail mid-transition needs a fixture corpus. It was mutation-checked: reversing the apply ordering makes it fail with the intended message.

The backup projection write after canonical Agentgres admission now says the admission stands and the divergence is replayable, instead of reporting a bare persist failure that reads as though the backup never happened.
still_open: NOT adopted onto the shared owner-scoped boundary. This plane still uses its own `append`/`admit_required` wrappers. They do bind authenticated scopes and do CAS, but they are a second implementation of the same contract, which is what the shared boundary exists to prevent. This gap stays OPEN for that reason alone.
No test drives cancellation or apply through an actual interrupted restore; the ordering is pinned by source assertion only.
Exact retry after restart is unproven for this plane.

open_gaps.plane: Foundry recipe, program, checkpoint, and qualification execution
open_gaps.gap: The plane already binds owner scopes and admits its primary state through Agentgres, but retains caller-side history/idempotency scanning and a direct admission wrapper rather than inheriting the shared discipline. Artifact/filesystem effects and multi-record run outputs need explicit orphan cleanup or recovery obligations when admission fails after bytes are materialized.
acceptance: remove caller-side idempotency scans and use the shared whole-stream enforcement
bind every artifact effect to an admitted intent and cleanup obligation
prove same-key/different-bytes, stale-head, restart replay, and post-materialization admission-failure recovery
progress: handle_recipe_run materialized the dataset artifact BEFORE binding the dataset's owner scope, so a snapshot ref already owned by another tenant was detected only after this daemon had written the artifact for it. The bind now precedes the write. The ref is content-addressed, so no corruption was possible either way and the bytes are identical — but an authorization refusal now costs no disk, and the effect follows the authorization that permits it.
open_gaps.correction: The gap text's first acceptance item — 'remove caller-side idempotency scans' — was written as though those scans were unsound. They were read and they are NOT. Both compare COMPLETE request identity: the recipe scan's content_hash is a JCS digest of the entire request minus expected_head and idempotency_key, and ProgramActionRequest has exactly three fields, of which action_identity carries the only two that are semantic. Neither can accept a same-key request with different bytes as a replay. They remain worth removing because each reads the WHOLE stream history per call — O(history) per program step, so O(n^2) across a long training run — and because a second definition of request identity beside the substrate's is exactly what the shared boundary exists to eliminate. That is a duplication and scaling argument, not a correctness one, and this gap should not be cited as evidence of a live idempotency defect.
still_open: NOT adopted onto the shared owner-scoped boundary; the plane keeps its own append/authorize_scope/bind_scope wrappers and its own idempotency scans.

Artifact effects still have no explicit cleanup obligation when admission fails after bytes are materialized. The exposure is bounded — artifacts are content-addressed and durable_write is a no-op when the bytes already match, so a retry converges and nothing is corrupted — but an unreferenced blob can still outlive a failed admission with nothing recording that it should be collected.
Same-key/different-bytes, stale-head, restart replay and post-materialization admission-failure recovery are unproven by test for this plane.

handler_level_classification.method: MEF-GAP-001's discriminator, MECHANIZED per handler rather than hand-maintained: (1) a SUCCESS response is reachable after a discarded write, AND (2) the written record kind is read back as state elsewhere. Superseding the hand-built list because it drifted in both directions — see classifier_coverage_defect. Still a CANDIDATE SET: each handler needs its own reading before it is called a defect. The handler count is EXPOSURE and double-counts by design (one shared helper is reached by many handlers); distinct_write_sites is the actionable unit.
sample_verified_by_hand: authority_routes::handle_authority_grant — takes no headers at all, discards the authority-grant write, and returns the grant with a live status and an expiry. `authority-grants` is read back by preflight, so a caller can be told `granted` while no later check can find the grant; a `denied` decision that fails to write leaves no audit trail, in a handler whose own comment claims a complete one.
binding_routes::handle_binding_create — discards the session-execution-binding write and returns a binding carrying a receipt_ref and a state_root_ref. `load_binding` reads that kind back.
handler_level_classification.reading_note: 84 handlers meet both tests and remain UNFIXED (was 92; the connector credential/authority-posture family in lifecycle_routes is closed). That is a CLASSIFIED CANDIDATE SET, not 84 confirmed defects: each still needs its own reading before it is called one. The 29 in `partial_fail_path_needs_reading` have some checked failure path in the handler and cannot be judged mechanically at all. The 7 whose record kind is never read back are the closest thing here to genuinely benign. CORRECTION 2026-08-07: this note previously read '94' and '8' against totals of 92 and 7; the totals were right (92+29+7=128) and the prose was stale.

classifier_coverage_defect.defect: Test (1) of the discriminator — 'returns success carrying a record whose only write was discarded' — was mechanized as though the response body must EMBED the written record. Handlers that return a CLAIM ABOUT the record instead were missed, and they are equally defective.
missed_handlers: lifecycle_routes::handle_connector_oauth_start — discards the sealed PKCE verifier write, then returns an authorize_url the operator visits for a flow the callback can no longer complete
lifecycle_routes::handle_connector_oauth_callback — returns {ok:true, connected:true} while discarding BOTH the credential write and the auth-posture write
lifecycle_routes::handle_connector_device_start — discards the sealed device_code write, then returns a user_code and verification_uri for a flow poll cannot complete
lifecycle_routes::handle_connector_device_poll — byte-for-byte the same defect as oauth_callback: {ok:true, connected:true} over two discarded writes

lifecycle_routes::handle_scim_group_delete — discards remove_record's bool entirely (not even `let _ =`) and returns 204, so a failed group delete is indistinguishable from success and the group's membership grants stay live

governance_routes::handle_approval_create / release_create / cohort_create / kill_create / gate_create — five creates discarded their writes and were absent from the census while the matching patches were listed; the KillSwitch record is read back by handle_kill_enforce
governance_routes::handle_cohort_patch — discarded, and absent while the other four patches in the same module were listed
classifier_coverage_defect.consequence: Five handlers across two already-audited families were absent from the census. The remaining rows are a floor, not a ceiling; re-run the classification with test (1) widened to cover success claims about a record, not only embedded records, and with bare discarded bools (remove_record) treated as indicators alongside `let _ = persist_record`.
classifier_coverage_defect.also_reclassified: lifecycle_routes::handle_connector_invoke writes a connector-invoke-receipt and returns it, but `connector-invoke-receipts` is read back NOWHERE, so it fails test (2) and is not a both-tests defect. It is not best-effort telemetry either — it is the audit record of a wallet-gated host mutation. It must not fail the call closed, because the host effect has already happened and cannot be un-invoked; the write result is now surfaced as `receipt_durable` instead of swallowed.
classifier_coverage_defect.resolution:
RESOLVED 2026-08-08 by mechanizing the discriminator in scripts/audit-daemon-mutation-handlers.mjs and wiring npm run check:mutation-handlers, so this list can no longer drift silently. Three distinct causes were found once it was mechanized, and all three had been invisible to hand maintenance:
  1. IMPLICIT 200. A handler declared `-> Json<Value>` returns 200 with no StatusCode and often no `ok:true` at all. Requiring an explicit success marker missed handle_binding_create — one of the two handlers this gap had ALREADY hand-verified as a defect.
  2. INTERPROCEDURAL WRITES. A discarded write is just as lost inside a helper the handler calls. Scanning only handler bodies missed five, including handle_editor_service_create via save_service. The classifier now takes the transitive closure over local calls.
  3. A SCANNER BUG IN THE CHECKER ITSELF. Rust char literals containing a double-quote (`.trim_matches('"')`) were parsed as string openers, blanking large regions of real code and hiding whole handler signatures. This one is worth recording because the checker's first version reported false negatives against handlers it had already been shown — a checker that answers wrongly is worse than no checker, and it was caught only by testing it against known cases rather than trusting its output.
registry_false_positives: handle_editor_services_list — a pure list handler: read_record_dir then Json(..). It contains no write of any kind and never did.

handler_level_classification.classified_disposition_marker: A discarded write whose tolerance is a RECORDED DECISION carries `CLASSIFIED` in a comment directly above it, and the checker excludes it while still counting it. MEF-GAP-001's acceptance explicitly allows 'intentionally best-effort' as an outcome, so a gate with no way to express its own allowed outcomes could never go green. It also stops the call-graph closure dragging in read-only handlers: handle_policies_get merely calls ensure_policy_seed, whose tolerated bootstrap write is classified at its own site.

progress: The gap asked for a handler-level classification instead of module-name grandfathering, and that classification now exists above. 284 census indicators resolve to 128 handlers with discarded writes: 92 meet both halves of the discriminator, 29 carry some checked failure path and cannot be judged mechanically, and 7 write a record kind nothing reads back.

authority_routes is CLOSED and now has zero discarded writes — it was the most severe module in the set and was fixed rather than merely catalogued. handle_authority_grant took no headers, discarded the grant write, and returned a live status with an expiry: a caller could be told `granted` while no preflight could find the grant, and a `denied` decision left no audit trail under a comment promising a complete one. Both revoke paths — the handler and the port-preview unexpose helper — emitted a `revoked` receipt and then discarded the write, so revocation reported success, produced evidence, and left the grant live and usable. emit_receipt returned a receipt ref it had not necessarily written, so grants could cite authority_receipt_refs resolving to nothing. issue_capability_lease and handle_harness_binding_create both returned records asserting admission over writes that could silently fail.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 — the connector credential and authority-posture family in lifecycle_routes: register, bind_credential, revoke_credential, set_policy, oauth_discover, oauth_start, oauth_callback, device_start, device_poll, and the SCM trio (register, bind_credential, revoke_credential). Twelve handlers, sixteen previously-discarded writes, now zero in the family. The two most severe: set_policy discarded the org-policy write while the invoke crossing refuses on org_policy.risk_posture == 'locked' and gates on principal_scoped, so an operator could lock an integration, be told it was locked, and leave it fully invokable; and both revoke paths reported a revoked posture over a discarded write, under a doc comment promising 'no fake ack'. remove_record returns remove_file(..).is_ok(), which conflated 'nothing was bound' with 'deletion failed' — both revoke paths now distinguish them and refuse when a present credential could not be removed. Fix shape matches each handler's existing failure convention rather than introducing a second one: typed 500 where the handler already returns (StatusCode, Json), ok:false where its whole convention is Json<Value> — the resource_routes::handle_allocate and authority_routes precedents respectively.

PROVEN AGAINST A LIVE DAEMON, not only by test — set_policy under an unwritable connector record refuses connector_org_policy_persistence_failed and leaves the on-disk risk_posture at its prior value; connector revoke refuses connector_auth_posture_persistence_failed; register against an unwritable directory returns HTTP 500 connector_registration_persistence_failed; SCM revoke refuses scm_connector_auth_posture_persistence_failed. Failures were induced by making the record file or its directory read-only, so these are real io::Error paths rather than injected ones.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 — the identity provisioning family in lifecycle_routes: oidc_set, scim_user_patch, scim_user_delete, scim_group_create, scim_group_patch, scim_group_delete. This is the most severe class found so far. Principal `status == "active"` IS the authentication gate, and SCIM DELETE returned 204 — the IdP's signal that deprovisioning completed and must never be retried — over a discarded write, so a terminated principal kept authenticating while the IdP recorded offboarding as done. scim_user_patch was worse in one respect: it swept the user's sessions AFTER the discarded principal write, so the observable result was cleared sessions and a still-active principal free to log straight back in; the refusal now fires BEFORE the sweep so a failure leaves coherent, retryable state. oidc_set is the SSO trust anchor (issuer, client id, sealed secret, and the `enabled` flag that decides whether OIDC login is accepted at all). Group membership is an access grant, and group_delete discarded remove_record's bool outright.

PROVEN AGAINST A LIVE DAEMON — with the principal record made read-only: SCIM DELETE returns HTTP 500 with a SCIM-shaped error instead of 204; PATCH active:false returns 500 instead of 200; the on-disk status remains `active` with no partial session sweep; and with the record writable again DELETE returns 204 and the status becomes `deactivated`. Real io::Error paths, induced by file permissions rather than injected.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 — capability_lease_plan_routes: plan_create, plan_patch, plan_revoke, plus plan_delete's receipt. `plan_receipt` returned a receipt_ref after discarding its own write and that ref was then embedded in the plan's history and receipt_refs — the exact defect authority_routes was closed for, where emit_receipt returned a ref it had not necessarily written. It now returns Option and the create/patch/revoke callers refuse when the receipt does not land. The plan record itself is re-read by the execution ladder at the moment of execution (connector_execution_routes: 'Ladder re-check at the moment of execution — never cached'), so returning the in-memory record as admitted state over a lost write handed the caller a plan later reads would not agree with. Zero discarded persists remain in the module. The refusal receipts in `bad` and the patch-rejected path are CLASSIFIED as deliberately tolerant audit rather than fixed: the refusal is returned either way, no state changes, and no receipt_ref reaches the caller — escalating a validation 400 into a 500 because an audit write failed would report the wrong defect. plan_delete cannot fail closed (the deletion already happened) so its receipt durability is surfaced as receipt_durable.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 — governance_routes, all ten control writes (approval, release, cohort, kill switch, gate; create and patch each). Zero discarded persists remain in the module. The severe one is the kill switch: handle_kill_enforce reloads the record and refuses unless state == 'tripped', so a trip returned over a discarded write reported the switch tripped while the record stayed armed — and enforcement would then refuse it with kill_switch_not_tripped. A safety control that reports engaged and cannot be enforced. Six of the ten were absent from the census; see classifier_coverage_defect.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 — the provider ACCOUNT plane in provider_routes: account_create, account_patch, credential bind, credential_revoke, and preflight. provider_receipt_ext returned a receipt_ref String after discarding its own write; it now returns Option<String>, so a non-durable receipt serializes as null instead of a ref that resolves to nothing, and the account-plane callers refuse outright. Revocation was the severe path: provider operations resolve credentials through load_account_credential against the vault, NOT through the account's status, so vault removal is the actual revocation — and `removed` conflated 'no credential was bound' with 'removal failed' while ok:true was returned unconditionally, so a credential that could not be deleted was reported revoked and stayed fully resolvable. Preflight is what moves an account to `verified`, and the patch handler relies on that stored verdict to know when posture must be re-proven.

PROVEN AGAINST A LIVE DAEMON — with the KillSwitch record read-only, PATCH transition=trip refuses governance_persistence_failed and the on-disk state remains `armed`; with the record writable the same call returns ok:true and the disk reads `tripped`.

CENSUS CORRECTED 2026-08-08. The hand-maintained list said 68; mechanizing the discriminator finds 138 handlers meeting both tests across 178 distinct write sites. The list was wrong in BOTH directions: it under-counted by missing implicit-200 handlers and writes held in helpers, and it over-counted by listing two handlers that contain no write at all. The classifier is now tracked tooling with a --check mode, validated against ground truth — every handler this program has already fixed is correctly absent from its output, and it independently caught a discarded one-time-consume this program had missed in the OAuth callback.

CLOSED 2026-08-08 — lifecycle_routes::handle_budget_set, the deployment-local budget policy. Canonical owner: components/hypervisor/identity-access-and-metering.md, which owns 'the deployment-local meter and budget enforcement projection' and defines Budget as 'a ceiling + a wallet-backed auto-funding policy'. Selected because it is a single canonical write with no receipt and no second effect: one singleton record ('budget'/'policy'), and nothing happens before the write, so a failed write needs no compensation and cannot strand a durable false-success receipt the way a receipt-before-record handler would. handle_budget_reconcile reads this policy to decide whether to replenish from wallet.network, so returning ok:true over a discarded write reported auto_fund_enabled:false as applied while funding continued — a spend control reported disengaged that keeps spending. The write behaviour is extracted into apply_budget_policy_update so its failure path is directly testable, and handle_budget_set is now only the Axum adapter. A failed persist returns HTTP 500 ok:false budget_policy_persistence_failed and the prior policy stands; a durable persist returns HTTP 200 acknowledged from the RELOADED projection, never from the in-memory candidate. CLOSES completion properties 5 (no success response before required durability confirmation) and 7 (typed recovery for ambiguous persistence failure) FOR THIS HANDLER ONLY.

PROVEN BY DETERMINISTIC, UID-INDEPENDENT FAULT INJECTION — lifecycle_routes::budget_policy_durability_tests calls the extracted production function directly. On the unpromoted daemon-file path that 'budget' takes today, persist_record can fail only at create_dir_all or at fs::write — a promoted family would admit through the substrate engine instead and its failure points would differ — and both faults are PATH SHADOWS rather than permission bits: a regular file where the family directory belongs (genesis), and a directory at the write target while the prior policy stays readable from a differently-named file in the same family — load_budget matches on id == 'policy', not on filename (successor). Disabling auto-funding under the successor fault returns HTTP 500 with the typed code while load_budget still reports auto_fund_enabled: true, which asserts the enforcement consequence rather than only the response shape. A durable write returns HTTP 200 and a re-read agrees with the acknowledgement. chmod is deliberately NOT used: root bypasses mode-bit denial, so a chmod-based fault would make these assertions pass vacuously whenever the suite runs as root.

CLOSED 2026-08-08 — ioi_agent_routes, the agent launch-policy and rollout plane. The severe pair is promote/rollback: rollback sets status=disabled as an explicit fail-closed, so a discarded write left the rolled-back variant ACTIVE and still overlay-selected — the operator is told the bad variant is withdrawn while it keeps serving. Three helpers were returning success-shaped values over swallowed writes and are now honest: set_rollout returns None, rollout_receipt returns Option<String> instead of a ref that resolves to nothing, and patch_release_control returns bool and is #[must_use]. policies_delete reported `deleted` for a policy it had just loaded and failed to remove. The launch record's `prepared` write happens BEFORE execution and now fails closed; the two post-execution outcome writes cannot, since the invocations have already run, so they surface outcome_durable instead.

NOT CLAIMED FOR handle_budget_set — six of the eight completion properties remain unsatisfied, and this packet changed none of them. Property 1 (authenticated principal, exact owner/tenant scope): lifecycle handlers do not each call authorize; the daemon's inbound auth middleware covers every /v1/* route only when authentication policy is enforced, and that enforcement is policy-gated with default OFF, so this handler establishes no explicit authenticated owner/tenant scope of its own. Property 2 (caller-owned idempotency key): absent. Property 3 (expected-absent genesis or expected-head compare-and-swap): absent, and handle_budget_reconcile performs an unguarded read-modify-write against the SAME 'budget'/'policy' singleton, so a concurrent set and reconcile silently clobber one another. Property 4 (Agentgres-admitted operation and hash-linked receipt): 'budget' is in neither PROMOTED_DOMAINS nor REQUIRED_ADMISSION_DOMAINS, so this remains a direct daemon-file write emitting no admitted operation, receipt, or event, and the current path admits none of these facts through Agentgres. Property 6 (restart replay from durable admitted truth): absent. Property 8 (cross-principal receipt and idempotency-key borrowing refusal): absent. Field validation is likewise unchanged: the handler still accepts any f64 for budget_ocu, threshold_ocu and target_ocu, and this packet deliberately did not alter validation.

handle_budget_reconcile remains OPEN and was deliberately not touched. It writes two kinds ('ledgers' then 'budget') and performs the funding effect itself, so it needs the already-happened-effect classification rather than a reflexive fail-closed. Recording that here so a later packet does not fail it closed by reflex.

SEPARATE AND LARGER, FOUND 2026-08-07 AND NOT CLAIMED FIXED — CapabilityLease plan revocation is unenforced. `handle_plan_revoke` now durably records status=revoked, but NO downstream consumer refuses on it: connector_execution_routes, connector_session_routes and materializing_run_routes contain zero references to `revoked`, while connector_execution_routes re-reads the plan at the moment of execution specifically to re-check the ladder. Revocation is therefore cosmetic even when the write lands. This is an authorization-semantics change, not a mutation-admission fix, and it is the same shape as the authority_routes residue (writes fail closed, routes remain unauthenticated). Fix before any claim that lease revocation works.
